pairs.subject: trust-base
pairs.evidence: e2e/guide.spec.ts:16 JSON.parse returns TypeScript's unchecked `any`, and it goes into an unannotated binding whose members are read on the next lines, so this is a trust-base member with no spelling at the call site that no directive or `as` census would count. Its practical harm is small, because each read goes straight into a runtime `expect`.

techniques.evidence: e2e/guide.spec.ts:17 This is the unsafe member access on the `any` from line 16. The value was never decoded into `unknown` and checked, which is the removal step the technique asks for. Text census over the 12 files: 1 unspelled decoder member (guide.spec.ts:16), plus spelled `as unknown as` assertions at review-undo.spec.ts:75 and :85.

e2e/review-undo.spec.ts:85 This double assertion depends on a global that the same test writes ten lines above (line 75) with the same restated shape. The dependency is local and adjacent, not on a distant declaration, so the technique's precondition does not hold.

pairs.registryProposal: census-counts-unmarked-members should say whether an `any` value read only to feed a test assertion library (whose matchers take unknown and re-check at runtime) counts as a member at the same weight as one flowing into production typed code. The lint predicate counts it, but the soundness exposure is close to nil.
